messages:
Priya (Support): Hi team — customer ACME Inc says objects that should have been deleted by their 30d custom retention are still showing up in search/embeddings in their US region even though their deletion API returned 200. They provided one example: obj-987654321. They’re asking for an urgent explain+mitigation because legal is looking into a data-removal compliance request.

Arjun (CustEng): Can you paste the raw repro steps they used? API call, region, and the audit event id if available. Also whether they used default retention or a per-bucket policy.

Priya (Support): Their steps: 1) create object in eu-west-1 on 2025-07-01, 2) set custom retention to 30d via `PATCH /v1/objects/obj-987654321` with `retention_days:30`, 3) on 2025-08-01 they called `DELETE /v1/objects/obj-987654321?region=eu-west-1` and got `200`. Audit shows: `event_id: ev-20250801-ACME-1122, actor: api-key-xxxx, action: object.delete, result: success`. But searching from a US region SDK returns the object in results and embeddings still match the content. They attached a screenshot of search result and embedding match id.

Kai (SRE): Two quick suspects: 1) indexer/search replication lag (indexer-worker-eu -> replicator-us), 2) stale cache in the read side (CDN/metadata cache or embeddings cache). Did they query via the same storage API or via our search/embeddings endpoints?

Priya (Support): They hit the hosted search API in us-east-1 and our embeddings endpoint in us-east-1. They said hitting `GET /v1/objects/obj-987654321?region=eu-west-1` returns 404 for the object metadata, but search/embeddings still return the content.

Leah (Infra): That pattern points to an eventual-consistency between storage and the secondary indexes. Delete tombstone landed in primary storage (hence 404), but the indexer/replicator pipeline might have still queued a pre-delete document or failed to process the tombstone. Check indexer logs around `ev-20250801-ACME-1122` and the `indexer-worker-eu-03` stream. Also confirm any backlog in `replicator-us-01` spool.

Arjun (CustEng): Can we get the audit log entry for the indexer pipeline? Priya, please request from customer the correlation id returned in the delete response (X-Request-Id) — we need that to trace through indexer + replicator logs.

Priya (Support): Asked the customer for X-Request-Id and they gave `req_0a9f3c`. Adding it here. They also mentioned they saw a `502` against `indexer.eu.internal` for ~30s around the delete time (screenshot).

Kai (SRE): If indexer had intermittent 5xx, tombstone might have failed to apply to the search index. Our normal fallback is to requeue, but if replication continued from an older snapshot the US index could have re-populated the doc. I'll grep logs for `req_0a9f3c` across indexer/replicator.

delete-bot: Automated note: deletion event ev-20250801-ACME-1122 recorded in audit log store at 2025-08-01T14:02:18Z. Tombstone written to storage shard s-eu-07.

Leah (Infra): Also check KMS key used for that object — if the key was being rotated or temporarily unavailable to the indexer, the indexer may have skipped decrypt+index steps. KMS events around 2025-08-01T14:02 are: `kms-rotate-start` on key `key-acme-prod-eu`, but we need to confirm whether that impacted indexer.

Marta (Legal): From a compliance POV, until search/embeddings are also purged, this is sensitive. If there's a chance of cross-region visibility, we should treat this as a hold/mitigation item. Do we have a safe temporary mitigation (like disable search results for that customer or add a filter) while we investigate?

Arjun (CustEng): Short-term actions: 1) Kai/Leah — confirm whether indexer replay or reindex will remove item from US index; if not, run targeted delete in the search index for doc id `obj-987654321` and embeddings store key `embed-obj-987654321`. 2) Priya — ask customer to avoid queries that return the object while we remediate. 3) Marta — advise if we should treat this as a legal hold incident (I think not yet, but keep in loop).

Kai (SRE): I found `req_0a9f3c` in indexer logs: indexer returned 502 for a short window, tombstone requeued at `indexer-queue-12`, but `replicator-us-01` shows a replay job on 2025-08-02 that repopulated from snapshot `snap-20250731-idx`. Looks like a race: snapshot-based replicator pulled a pre-delete snapshot and reapplied documents to US.

Leah (Infra): Confirmed KMS rotation occurred but did not fail decryption for tombstone operations. So KMS is likely not root cause. Root looks like replicator snapshot timing.

Arjun (CustEng): Proposed remediation: 1) run targeted delete on US search index + embeddings now (safest). 2) schedule a reindex pass for ACME account to ensure no stale docs. 3) add a short-term guard: replicator should check tombstone marker version before applying snapshot docs (bugfix).

Marta (Legal): OK please do targeted delete and confirm with me when completed. Also log this as an incident with severity = P2 (potential compliance exposure).

Priya (Support): Noted. I will coordinate the targeted delete and ask for a confirmation screenshot for Legal. ETA for delete job is ~30m. Will post back when done. :white_check_mark:

Arjun (CustEng): Thanks, team. After remediation let's add an entry to the runbook: cross-region snapshot replay can reintroduce deleted docs — include detection steps (audit id -> indexer queue -> replicator snapshot), and a mitigation checklist.

Kai (SRE): I’ll keep the `replicator-us-01` job paused for ACME until the reindex completes. Posting logs to the incident channel once done.

Priya (Support): Update: targeted delete job completed at 2025-08-01T15:01Z. Customer confirmed search results no longer return `obj-987654321`. Sending closure note to customer and cc'ing Legal.

Marta (Legal): Received. Please attach audit evidence (delete request + index delete job id) to the incident record.

Priya (Support): Uploaded evidence to the incident ticket: `inc-20250801-ACME-45`. Closing thread unless anyone wants follow-up.
